text: A man stood on a railroad bridge in northern Alabama, looking down into the swift water twenty feet below, his hands tied behind his back. <break time="0.8s" /> A rope around his neck was fastened to a beam above his head, and he stood on a loose board laid across the railroad ties. <break time="0.8s" /> Two Union soldiers and their sergeant stood beside him on the board, and nearby stood a captain, who watched quietly with his arms folded. <break time="0.8s" /> At each end of the bridge stood a guard with his rifle held straight up in front of his chest. <break time="0.8s" /> The man who was about to die was about thirty five years old, and he was dressed like a rich planter, not like a soldier. <break time="0.8s" /> When he closed his eyes to think of his wife and children, a sharp, ringing sound like a hammer striking iron broke into his thoughts. <break time="0.8s" /> It was only the ticking of his watch, but each tick seemed slower and louder than the one before. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a wild hope came to him that he might free his hands, throw off the rope, and swim home to his family. <break time="0.8s" /> Just as these thoughts flashed through his mind, the captain nodded to the sergeant, and the sergeant stepped off the board.
